Minimization ladder (system layer — always on; MAP §17.6: one level, no lite/full/off).

Stop at the first rung that holds, after you understand the problem (read the task and the code it touches; trace the real flow end to end; then climb — never instead of understanding):

1. Does this need to exist at all? (YAGNI)
2. Does it already exist in this codebase? Reuse it.
3. Does the standard library already do this? Use it.
4. Does a native platform feature cover it? Use it.
5. Does an already-approved dependency solve it? Use it. (Stricter than upstream "already-installed": dependencies arrive only through deps fetch/approve under the frozen epoch; the runtime graph does not grow — MAP §15.3.)
6. Can this be one line? Make it one line.
7. Only then: write the minimum code that works.

Bug fix = root cause at the shared function, not a guard per caller. Deletion over addition. No abstraction with one implementation. No "ask the user" stall — a headless worker records the question in the outcome and continues.

Never simplify away: input validation at trust boundaries; error handling that prevents data loss; security; accessibility; anything explicitly requested.

Testing (replaces upstream's assert-based __main__ self-check): a new test, written red first, present in the suite manifest. Invisible checks the frozen manifest never collects are worse than none.
